english: Who wrote this letter?
tip: A final p often softens to b before a vowel suffix: 'mektup' plus '-u' becomes 'mektubu', the object form of letter.

english: Mehmet left the newspaper at the post office.
tip: A vowel-final noun adds a buffer y before the object suffix: 'gazete' plus '-i' becomes 'gazeteyi', not 'gazetei'.

english: Open the window, it's very hot.
tip: ‘Pencereyi’ aç uses the bare verb stem as a command: ‘aç’ = open, from ‘açmak’ with no ending.

english: Maybe we can meet some other time.
tip: Insert '-abil' into a verb for 'can, be able': 'buluş' plus '-abil' plus '-iriz' gives 'buluşabiliriz', we can meet.

english: I met with my friends at the swimming pool.
tip: Suffixes stack in order: 'arkadaşlarımla' is 'arkadaş' plus '-lar' plural plus '-ım' my plus '-la' with, so with my friends.

target: Çocuklar bütün öğleden sonra bahçede oynadı.
english: The children played in the garden all afternoon.
tip: A plural subject can take a singular verb: 'çocuklar oynadı', the children played, needs no '-lar' on 'oynadı'.

target: Doktor bana daha fazla su içmemi söyledi.
english: The doctor told me to drink more water.
tip: To report a command, use the '-me' form plus 'söylemek': 'içmemi söyledi' means told me to drink, where '-mi' marks my drinking.

target: Arkadaşım bu sabah telefon etti sonra dışarı çıktı.
english: My friend called this morning and then went outside.
tip: 'etmek' turns a noun into a verb: 'telefon etti' means made a phone, that is, called.

english: When did you come to Istanbul?
tip: A proper noun takes an apostrophe before a case suffix: 'İstanbul'a' means to Istanbul.

english: Our kitchen is small but practical.
tip: A final k usually softens to ğ before a vowel suffix: 'mutfak' plus '-ımız' becomes 'mutfağımız', our kitchen.

english: The children ride their bicycles after school.
tip: 'After' uses the source suffix '-dan' plus 'sonra': 'okuldan sonra' means after school.

english: Thanks to technology, distance education became widespread.
tip: 'sayesinde' means 'thanks to' and follows its noun: 'teknoloji sayesinde' means thanks to technology.

english: I brought home the dog I saw on the street.
tip: A describing clause comes before its noun via '-düğüm': 'gördüğüm köpek' means the dog that I saw.

target: Otobüs beklerken kitabımdan birkaç sayfa okudum.
english: While waiting for the bus, I read a few pages of my book.
tip: The suffix '-ken' means 'while': 'beklerken' means while waiting, setting the scene for the main action.

target: Bu restoranın etli ekmeği çok meşhur olmuş.
english: This restaurant's meat bread has become very famous.
tip: The '-miş' past reports something inferred or just noticed: 'meşhur olmuş' means it has apparently become famous.

english: I sip patiently.
tip: 'sabırla' = 'sabır' (patience) + 'la': the '-la/-le' ending turns a noun into 'with X', so 'sabırla' means patiently.

english: I didn't understand anything at the market.
tip: 'market' ends in the hard consonant t, so 'in the market' hardens '-de' to '-te': 'markette', never 'marketde'.

english: I'm sorry, I'm late.
tip: 'geç kaldım' = I was late: Turkish pairs 'geç' (late) with 'kalmak' (to stay), literally 'I stayed late'.

english: Thank you, you are very kind.
tip: 'naziksiniz' = 'nazik' + 'siniz': attach '-siniz' straight to an adjective for the formal 'you are'. No separate verb needed.

english: Everyone liked the song very much.
tip: 'şarkıyı' = 'şarkı' + 'yı': a specific object takes the object suffix '-ı', with a buffer y after the vowel. The particular song.

english: The neighbors sold vegetables in the garden.
tip: 'komşular' is plural but the verb stays singular: 'sattı', not 'sattılar'. Turkish plural noun subjects normally take a singular verb.

english: I didn't read the book, I didn't have time.
tip: 'okumadım' = 'oku' (read) + 'ma' (not) + 'dı' (past) + 'm' (I). Past negatives stack root, then not, then tense, then person.

english: We drive to work together.
tip: 'araba ile' = by car: the free word 'ile' means 'with' or 'by means of'. It can also stick on as '-yla', giving 'arabayla'.

english: Have a good journey, please drive carefully.
tip: 'sürün' is the polite command 'drive': add '-ün' to the stem 'sür' for formal or plural you. Casual singular is just 'sür'.

english: Could I get your phone number please?
tip: 'alabilir miyim' = may I get: '-abil' adds 'can/able' to the verb and the separate 'mi' turns it into a polite question.

english: The pilot went to the airport every morning.
tip: 'gitti' marks its destination with '-a/-e': 'havaalanına' = to the airport. Go-verbs use this ending, not a separate 'to'.

target: Ressam gelecek ay hastanede resim yapacak.
english: The painter will paint at the hospital next month.
tip: 'yapacak' = 'yap' + 'acak': the '-acak/-ecek' ending marks the future, so 'will paint'. 'gelecek ay' sets it next month.

target: Siyah kedi beyaz duvarın üstünde oturuyor.
english: The black cat is sitting on the white wall.
tip: 'duvarın üstünde' = on the wall: 'üst' (top) takes a possessive ending and the wall takes the owner-suffix '-ın', literally 'at the wall's top'.

target: Yemyeşil orman her mevsim ayrı güzel.
english: The lush green forest is beautiful in every season.
tip: 'yemyeşil' intensifies 'yeşil' (green): Turkish repeats the first sound with an added consonant for 'very', like 'masmavi'.

target: Ninem her akşam bize masal anlatırdı.
english: My grandmother used to tell us stories every evening.
tip: 'anlatırdı' = 'anlat' + 'ır' + 'dı': the habitual '-ır' plus past '-dı' means 'used to tell', a repeated habit in the past.
